summary: Exact recognition criterion in the ENTIRE original C/G: cozero rational sublevels and a uniform lower strict-obstacle majorant energy profile are equivalent to an actual decreasing finite-energy presentation. Target feasibility and equation existence remain unresolved.
detailedSummary: For bounded-above u, define Gamma_u(h) as the supremum of E(a) over actual original-C weights satisfying u<=a<h, and A(u) as its infimum over ordinary continuous strict upper obstacles. Original G membership is equivalent to cozero rational sublevels and A(u)>-infinity. Explicit continuous barriers and summable constant corrections construct the required actual decreasing C sequence. Continuous recognized functions are exactly C. Every mass-two positive Radon measure with finite FULL D has finite moment against a recognized u, with integral u>=A(u)-D. Neither recognition predicates for an isotropic target potential nor prescribed-equation existence are established.
text:
An exact recognition bridge in the ENTIRE original class.

Retain K=C((s)), |s|=exp(-1/8), t=s^8 and the supplied compact, good, strict, smooth, separated, boundaryless pure surface X=(Gm^2)^an/<(t,2),(3,t)>. Genuine nonalgebraization and coherent descent are NOT certified. Keep local rho=|r|^2/2, theta=DD rho and reference raw mass two. C is the ENTIRE minimal continuous CLD class of weights a with rho+a locally in the smallest continuous sheaf containing smooth positive-Hessian generators and closed under local uniform limits. G consists precisely of limits of ACTUAL continuous a_n in C decreasing everywhere, with inf E(a_n)>-infinity. Write theta_a=theta+DD a and E(a)=(1/3) integral a(theta^2+theta_a theta+theta_a^2). No operator or limiting energy is assigned to an unrepresented function.

For bounded-above u:X->[-infinity,infinity) and ordinary real continuous h>u everywhere, define Gamma_u(h)=sup{E(a):a in ENTIRE C, u<=a<h everywhere}, with sup empty=-infinity, and A(u)=inf_{h continuous,h>u}Gamma_u(h). A(u) is an obstacle-feasibility profile, not a definition of extended energy E(u). A cozero set is {f>0} for continuous f:X->[0,1].

THEOREM. u belongs to the ORIGINAL G if and only if every rational sublevel {u<q} is cozero and A(u)>-infinity. For real continuous u these conditions are equivalent to u in ORIGINAL C. For every positive Radon mu of raw mass two with FULL D(mu)=sup_ENTIRE_C(E(a)-integral a mu)<infinity, a recognized u has a finite moment and integral u mu>=A(u)-D(mu).

Bounded structural reconstruction. Constant addition preserves the minimal sheaf: for fixed c, continuous f for which f+c belongs to that sheaf form a uniformly closed sheaf containing its smooth positive-Hessian generators. Global uniform closure of C follows locally. CLD recursive products of actual continuous psh potentials are positive closed; their dpsh multilinear extension and invariance under smooth DD-null changes glue B(a,b)=theta_a wedge theta_b globally. Locally a=(rho+a)-rho is dpsh. The defining derivative identity gives B(a,b)-theta^2=DD(a theta_b)+DD(b theta). The global smooth test 1 has compact support on compact X and DD1=0. Evaluating these exact currents proves that every bounded mixed mass is two. Positive top currents are Radon, so E is real on C. Since theta_(a+c)=theta_a, E(a+c)=E(a)+2c. This uses no nonsmooth Green identity, energy concavity or generated-operator theorem.

Barrier proof. If ordinary continuous h_n decrease to u, then {u<q}=union_n{h_n<q}. The uniformly convergent continuous series f_q=sum_n 2^-n min(1,(q-h_n)_+) is positive exactly there. Conversely choose an integer M>=sup u and v=exp(u-M), with exp(-infinity)=0. For each rational q<M choose continuous f_q in [0,1] positive exactly on {u<q}. Put r_q=exp(q-M) and k_(q,j)=r_q+(1-r_q)(1-j f_q)_+, j>=1. Each is continuous, positive and dominates v: on u>=q it is one; on u<q it is at least r_q>v. At a point with u<M, rational q>u can approach u, or tend to -infinity at a pole, and large j makes k_(q,j)=r_q. At u=M all these functions are one. Their pointwise infimum is therefore v. Enumerate the countable pairs (q,j), take K_n to be their first-n minimum, and set h_n=M+log K_n. These are REAL continuous functions decreasing to u at EVERY point, including poles. Open rational sublevels prove upper semicontinuity. No metrizability or countable dense analytic test family is assumed.

Recognition proof, necessity. An actual a_n decreasing to u with E(a_n)>=L supplies cozero sublevels by the barrier proof. For fixed continuous h>u, the open sets {a_n<h} increase and cover compact X. A finite subcover gives one global n with u<=a_n<h. Thus Gamma_u(h)>=L for every obstacle and A(u)>=L.

Recognition proof, sufficiency. Obtain ordinary continuous h_n decreasing to u from the cozero condition. Choose real L<A(u), epsilon_n=2^(-n-2), and s_n=sum_(k>=n)epsilon_k=2^(-n-1). Under H_1=h_1+epsilon_1 choose actual b_1 in C with u<=b_1<H_1 and E(b_1)>L. For n>=2 set H_n=min(h_n+epsilon_n,b_(n-1)+epsilon_(n-1)). This is an ordinary continuous obstacle strictly above u. Since Gamma_u(H_n)>=A(u)>L, choose actual b_n in C with u<=b_n<H_n and E(b_n)>L. The minimum obstacle is NEVER declared psh. Set a_n=b_n+s_n. Then a_(n+1)<a_n because s_n=epsilon_n+s_(n+1); u<=a_n<h_n+epsilon_n+s_n; and E(a_n)=E(b_n)+2s_n>L. These actual globally continuous original-C weights decrease everywhere to u, including at poles, with the required lower energy bound.

Continuous corollary. Continuous u has barriers u+1/n. If u belongs to C, these are an actual presentation with energies E(u)+2/n. Conversely, actual a_n decreasing to real continuous u converge uniformly: for every positive delta the increasing open sets {a_n<u+delta} cover compact X, so one is all of X. Uniform closure puts u in C. This uses actual continuous tails.

Moment proof. For a admissible under h, FULL dual finiteness and positivity give E(a)<=D(mu)+integral h mu. Hence Gamma_u(h)<=D(mu)+integral h mu, also for an empty admissible set. A constant obstacle bounds A(u) above finitely; recognition bounds it below. Ordinary barriers h_n decreasing to u give strict obstacles h_n+1/n and A(u)<=D(mu)+integral h_n mu+2/n. Monotone convergence applied to h_1-h_n gives integral h_n->integral u, possibly initially -infinity. The real lower bound excludes -infinity and proves the claim. For an eligible whole Dirac this integral is 2u(x), so a recognized potential cannot have a pole at x. Constant translation gives Gamma_(u+c)(h+c)=Gamma_u(h)+2c and A(u+c)=A(u)+2c.
